https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/t.title_zh: 蒂努布：我会补贴农业生产，而不是燃料消费
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/t.body_zh: 第无数次，博拉·蒂努布总统宣布燃油补贴绝不会恢复，并斥责那些承诺恢复补贴的人为骗子。不过，他表示政府将补贴农业生产，而不是燃油消费。蒂努布周二在吉加瓦州的一次集会上表示，尼日利亚不能继续消耗子孙后代的未来，以维持一个正在耗尽国家资源的体系。总统说：“那些说补贴将恢复的人是在撒谎。别再让他们骗你们了。补贴不会恢复。我们不能今天花掉子女的未来，却指望他们明天继续生活。”那些认为应该恢复补贴的人都是骗子。你们拿什么支付那些承诺？拿什么修路？拿什么维护道路？又拿什么维持运转？“我们将补贴农业生产，奖励小规模农户。面向农户的无息贷款即将推出。繁荣即将到来。粮食安全将得到保障。”我希望你们听明白，尼日利亚。你们听到了吗，尼日利亚？面向小规模农户的无息贷款即将发放。我们将在六个地理区域设立机械化农业服务中心。推动机械化农业。”我们有可耕地，有决心，也有人才。我们能够养活自己，并会把食品价格降至最低。我向你们保证，我们将推动农业机械化、灌溉以及提高土地和可耕地的附加值。”蒂努布表示，大学将比以往任何时候都更深入参与农业研究与开发。总统感谢民众的忠诚和投入，同时承诺正面解决安全问题。他说：“我已经清楚听到了你们的诉求。我知道尼日利亚存在安全问题。但只要我们携手合作，作为你们的朋友和伙伴，你们掌握的任何安全信息都应立即上报。”我向你们保证，我们正努力确保尼日利亚安全，并妥善照顾我们的武装力量，为他们提供住房和奖励，不论他们来自哪里。我们将战胜不安全威胁。“我们经历过许多战争。我们将击败敌人，击败破坏团结的敌人、破坏稳定的敌人以及一切敌人。”总统指出，政府已经加强警察和武装力量，如今也为他们发放更高的薪资。总统称学生贷款计划NELFUND是反贫困的武器。他说：“我们通过设立NELFEND，解决子女的教育问题。NELFEND是反贫困的武器。你们同意吗？NELFEND是反贫困的武器。我们将继续沿着这个方向前进。”他宣布，经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）追回的全部违规资金如今都拨入NELFEND，用于儿童教育；追回的全部资产也将投入NELFEND。蒂努布赞扬吉加瓦州州长乌马尔·纳马迪，称自己从未见过一个人取得如此大的进展。他说：“我在这里已有许多年，从未见过一个人推动如此多的进展。这就是州长乌马尔·纳马迪。他为我们所有人不知疲倦、辛勤工作，让所有人共享民主的成果。”蒂努布宣布将为农户提供重大新支持，并宣称政府将补贴农业生产，而不是燃油消费。总统保证，政府将投资改善每个地方政府的医疗条件和发展机会。他进一步保证将降低生活成本、维护安全并提供可靠的电力。他说：“不是过去那种毫无成效的私有化。我们将在尼日利亚每个地区为你们提供可靠电力。”全进步大会党（APC）总统竞选委员会（PCC）总干事发言称，蒂努布在西北地区获得的大规模支持，戳穿了反对派所谓总统不会在尼日利亚北部受到欢迎的说法。亚里告诉总统，现场的群众——男人、女人和青年——证明西北地区与他站在一起。他补充说：“总统阁下，这些都是您的人民，男人、女人和青年。这里是西北地区，我们的对手正在竞选造势，说您不会在尼日利亚北部受到欢迎。”亚里强调，除了蒂努布担任州长和总统期间为尼日利亚及北部所做的贡献外，反对派拿不出任何其他东西。亚里要求那些自称为北方核心派的人指出，他们曾支持哪位候选人最终获胜。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，并在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，该报通过所有平台面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英及更广泛的中产阶层，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。这家报纸秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真理与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育、社区以及人与社会的交叉议题。您可以发送邮件至hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系页面

https://www.myjoyonline.com/gipa-ceo-cal.body: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Simon Madjie, has called for a shift from raw material exports towards value addition to accelerate Ghana’s industrial transformation. According to him, Ghana must leverage its mineral and cocoa resources to develop local industries, create jobs and strengthen control over its natural resources. He said moving beyond raw material exports by 2030 required deliberate efforts to attract investment and expand domestic processing capacity. According to him, natural resources should serve as a foundation for industrial development rather than being treated solely as commodities for export. Mr Madjie emphasised the importance of attracting international private capital, noting that investors were expected to pay taxes, create jobs, transfer technology and operate responsibly in exchange for access to Ghana’s markets and natural resources. He urged foreign investors to integrate Ghanaian businesses into their value chains to build local capacity and competitiveness. The GIPA CEO also highlighted the need for legal and regulatory reforms to strengthen investor protection and reduce barriers to doing business. However, he stressed that reforms must be supported by an enabling business environment that encouraged collaboration between local and foreign investors. He said stronger partnerships, technology transfer and local participation were essential to building Ghanaian businesses and sustaining long-term industrial growth
https://www.myjoyonline.com/gipa-ceo-cal.title_zh: 加纳投资促进中心首席执行官呼吁从原材料出口转向增值加工
https://www.myjoyonline.com/gipa-ceo-cal.body_zh: 加纳投资促进中心（GIPA）首席执行官Simon Madjie呼吁加纳从出口原材料转向发展增值产业，以加快加纳的工业转型。据他表示，加纳必须利用其矿产和可可资源发展本地产业、创造就业机会，并加强对自然资源的掌控。他说，要到2030年实现超越原材料出口的目标，就必须有意识地努力吸引投资并扩大国内加工能力。据他表示，自然资源应成为工业发展的基础，而不是仅仅被当作出口商品对待。Madjie先生强调吸引国际私人资本的重要性，指出投资者进入加纳市场和获取其自然资源的同时，应当纳税、创造就业岗位、转让技术并负责任地经营。他敦促外国投资者将加纳企业纳入其价值链，以建设本地能力和竞争力。GIPA首席执行官还指出，有必要推进法律和监管改革，以加强投资者保护并减少经营障碍。不过，他强调，改革必须得到有利的商业环境支持，而这种环境应鼓励本地与外国投资者之间的合作。他说，更紧密的伙伴关系、技术转让和本地参与对于建设加纳企业并维持长期工业增长至关重要。

https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editori.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny. In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations. https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editori.body_zh: 订阅账户还可享受 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinions 等更多内容。订阅即可解锁这些内容。纳坦迪尔邦政府突然解散有关联邦与邦关系的库里安·约瑟夫委员会，并将相关任务移交给泰米尔纳德邦法律委员会，这似乎表明，C. 约瑟夫·维贾伊政府屈从于推翻先前决定的政治冲动，而非受到任何充分理由或必要性的指导。从其提出的依据来看，这一点更加可信。该委员会以严谨的学术态度履行职责，其报告第一部分于2月提交给当时的M.K.斯大林政府。以委员会属于“非法定机构”为理由，难以令人信服，尤其是法律委员会本身也仅通过“行政命令”设立。此外，也没有公开证据表明邦法律委员会曾审查或处理过联邦与邦关系相关问题。委员会的任务是“就邦际关系及中央与邦关系提出办法和建议”，这只是8月重新组建的邦法律委员会更广泛职权范围的一部分。鉴于该委员会承担更广泛的职责，历届邦政府均设立过高级别委员会，审查涉及并行列表事项的冲突，并提出具体补救措施。泰米尔纳德邦正是依据这类建议，制定了若干立法，以克服中央法律施加的限制，包括在专业课程招生中为弱势学生实行横向保留政策。因此，该邦以委员会与法律委员会所获委托职能的“性质和范围存在相似或重叠”为由提出的另一项论点，经不起仔细推敲。9月，反对党领袖乌达亚尼迪·斯大林曾指出，有人企图“瘫痪”委员会的运作。公正评估委员会第一部分报告，可以看出其对邦自主权、边界划分和总督职位等议题进行了客观而深入的研究。除人民党外，各政党大多对报告表示欢迎。值得注意的是，报告内容与维贾伊先生所属泰米尔aga维特里卡扎甘公开的邦权利立场并不存在任何明显冲突。此外，委员会唯一一名公开具有政治关联的成员M.纳加纳丹教授早已辞职。政府不妨重新考虑，并允许委员会完成工作。这将有助于推动建立更加平衡的联邦治理结构，促进中央与邦之间的和谐关系。评论必须使用英文，并以完整句子表述。评论不得带有辱骂性或人身攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已是《The Hindu》注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与我们的文章讨论。如果你没有账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录账户后可在 Vuukle 查看过去的评论。

https://punchng.com/2027-ondo-apc-campai.summary: The Director-General of the Ondo State APC Presidential Campaign Council, Mr Victor Olabimtan, made the declaration while speaking with journalists in Akure, the state capital, on Tuesday. The APC chieftain said the party members across the 18 Local Government Areas of the state were already working towards achieving victory for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.
https://punchng.com/2027-ondo-apc-campai.summary_zh: 奥恩多州全进步大会党总统竞选委员会主任Victor Olabimtan先生周二在州首府阿库雷接受记者采访时宣布了这一消息。这位全进步大会党领导人表示，该州18个地方政府的党内成员已经行动起来，争取让总统Bola Tinubu在2027年再次当选时获胜。
https://punchng.com/2027-ondo-apc-campai.body: The Ondo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress has assured that the party would win the presidential, national and state assembly elections in the state. The Director-General of the Ondo State APC Presidential Campaign Council, Mr Victor Olabimtan, made the declaration while speaking with journalists in Akure, the state capital, on Tuesday. The APC chieftain said the party members across the 18 Local Government Areas of the state were already working towards achieving victory for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. Olabimtan added that the party would also win all seats across the state’s three senatorial districts, nine federal constituencies and 26-member House of Assembly. ”We will achieve our target of securing one million votes for President Bola Tinubu in Ondo State, as we have started the grassroots mobilisation strategy. 2027: Tinubu promises Nigerians reliable power supply 2027: APC unveils four-pillar manifesto for Tinubu’s second term bid Tinubu inaugurates reconstructed Lagos governor’s lodge in Abuja ”The party has mobilised 25 voters in each of its 3,962 polling units, with each person expected to bring five additional voters. The one-million-vote target is achievable, and by the grace of God, we are going to reach it,” he boasted. On the purported division in the party, Olabimtan said the party leadership had taken steps to reconcile aggrieved members, expressing confidence that the party would work together to secure victory for Tinubu and other candidates in the 2027 general elections. He added that the presidential campaign scheduled to hold in Akure on Wednesday would bring together all party leaders and members, saying the party had resolved its internal differences and was ready to present a united front ahead of the presidential rally. ”Although the APC family may appear divided from the outside, we know how to resolve our differences. Those differences are being addressed, and I assure you that we are campaigning together,” he said. He disclosed that after the rally, the state governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, would commence a campaign tour across the LGAs to be accompanied by candidates contesting the Senate, House of Representatives, and state House of Assembly elections. Peter Dada
https://punchng.com/2027-ondo-apc-campai.title_zh: 2027年：奥ND州全州APC竞选委员会誓言让蒂努布及其他候选人胜选
https://punchng.com/2027-ondo-apc-campai.body_zh: 全进步大会党（APC）奥多州分部保证，该党将在该州赢得总统选举、国民议会选举和州议会选举。奥多州APC总统竞选委员会主任维克托·奥拉比姆坦先生于周二在州首府阿库雷接受记者采访时发表了这一声明。这名APC党魁说，该州18个地方政府辖区的党员已经在为实现博拉·蒂努布总统2027年连任的目标而努力。奥拉比姆坦补充说，该党还将赢得该州3个选区的全部参议院席位、9个联邦选区席位以及由26名议员组成的州议会全部席位。“我们将在奥多州为博拉·蒂努布总统争取100万张选票，实现我们的目标，因为我们已经开始实施基层动员战略。2027年：蒂努布承诺为尼日利亚人提供可靠电力供应。2027年：APC公布支持蒂努布竞选第二任期的四大支柱宣言。蒂努布在阿布贾为重建后的拉各斯州长官邸揭幕。“该党已经在3,962个投票站中的每个投票站动员了25名选民，并预计每个人再带来5名选民。100万张选票的目标可以实现，蒙上帝恩典，我们将达到这一目标。”他自豪地说。谈到党内所谓的分歧，奥拉比姆坦表示，党领导层已经采取措施调解心怀不满的党员，并相信全党将在2027年大选中齐心协力，为蒂努布及其他候选人争取胜利。他补充说，定于周三在阿库雷举行的总统竞选集会将汇集全党所有领导人和党员，并称该党已经解决内部分歧，准备在总统集会前展现团结统一的阵容。“尽管APC这个大家庭从外面看可能显得分裂，但我们知道如何解决分歧。这些分歧正在得到处理，我向你们保证，我们正在并肩竞选。”他说。他透露，集会结束后，州长拉基·阿耶塔瓦将在各地方政府辖区展开竞选巡回，参议员、众议员和州议会选举的参选人将陪同他开展活动。彼得·达达

https://3news.com/crime/illegal-mining-b.summary: First, that illegal mining by Chinese nationals be treated as a bilateral enforcement priority, and that the framework agreed at the 2026 China Mining Conference — under which offenders will face sanctions not only in Ghana but also through Chinese authorities' own mechanisms for policing their citizens abroad — be operationalised without delay.
https://3news.com/crime/illegal-mining-b.summary_zh: 首先，应将中国公民非法采矿作为双方共同优先处理的执法事项，并立即将2026年中国矿业大会达成的框架付诸实施。根据该框架，违法者不仅会在加纳受到制裁，中国主管机关也会通过自身机制对其境外公民进行监管并实施制裁。
https://3news.com/crime/illegal-mining-b.body: Speaking at the China-Ghana Mining Cooperation Conference at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, Mr Tandoh said the integrity of the partnership between the two countries is being tested not in boardrooms, but in Ghana's rivers, forest reserves and farmlands. "Illegal small-scale mining has become an existential threat to our environment, our water bodies, and our national security. And in too many instances, Chinese nationals have been found at the centre of these illegal operations," he said. The conference was attended by the Chief of Staff, Dr Julius Debrah, the Chinese Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Cong Song, Ministers of State, President of the Ghana Chamber of Mines Fred Attakuma, CEO Dr Ken Ashigbey, industry captains, traditional leaders and members of the media. Mr Tandoh was unequivocal about the law. Under the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), as amended, small-scale mining licences are reserved exclusively for Ghanaian citizens. "That means any foreigner who undertakes small-scale mining commits an offence. The penalties include a prison term of twenty to twenty-five years, with deportation to follow the sentence," he said. He said the law also targets "fronting," where foreign entities use Ghanaians to acquire mineral rights, and disclosed that several Chinese nationals have been arrested during swoops on major rivers, including the Birim and the Tano. Despite the warning, Mr Tandoh praised Chinese investment in Ghana's large-scale mining sector, which he said had contributed to Ghana's position as Africa's largest gold producer and the world's sixth-largest. He cited major Chinese mining giants such as Zijin, Chifeng and Shandong, noting that Zijin, which assumed ownership of the Akyem mine a year ago, had increased production by 20% without expanding its workforce or upgrading infrastructure. He also said Shandong Gold's Ghanaian operation is the best-performing mine in the Shandong group globally. He said the Association of China-Ghana Mining has given the cooperation an institutional home for dialogue on responsible investment, regulatory compliance and sustainable development. "This is to ensure that while we protect the integrity of our bilateral relations, we also protect the credibility of our regulatory system for the future of our mining communities," he said. First, that illegal mining by Chinese nationals be treated as a bilateral enforcement priority, and that the framework agreed at the 2026 China Mining Conference — under which offenders will face sanctions not only in Ghana but also through Chinese authorities' own mechanisms for policing their citizens abroad — be operationalised without delay. "This dual-enforcement pathway must be operationalised without delay, so that deportation is not a soft landing but a prelude to accountability," he said. Second, that China work with Ghana to dismantle the financing and logistics networks that enable illegal mining, noting that galamsey is organised, financed and equipped, with equipment, capital and supply chains sometimes originating outside Ghana. Third, that the Association of China-Ghana Mining be used as a vehicle for compliance, not just commerce, by actively discouraging and reporting illegal conduct by its members and by Chinese nationals operating in Ghana. "A responsible association does not protect the lawlessness, it exposes them," he said. Mr Tandoh said the Minerals Commission will continue to enforce the law without fear or favour, while working with investors who share its vision of a transparent and sustainable mining industry. "Ghana values China's friendship too deeply to allow it to be undermined by the conduct of a lawless minority. And China's own reputation as a responsible global investor is too valuable to be tarnished by the actions of those who operate outside the law," he said
https://3news.com/crime/illegal-mining-b.title_zh: 中国人的非法采矿威胁加纳与中国的友谊
https://3news.com/crime/illegal-mining-b.body_zh:
2026年11月10日星期二，在阿克拉凯宾斯基酒店举行的中国—加纳矿业合作会议上，Tandoh先生表示，两国伙伴关系的诚信考验不在会议室里，而在加纳的河流、森林保护区和农田中。他说：“非法小规模采矿已成为我们环境、水体和国家安全的生存性威胁。而在太多情况下，中国公民被发现处于这些非法活动的核心。”

加纳总统府办公厅主任Julius Debrah博士、中国驻加纳大使Cong Song阁下、国务部长、加纳矿业商会会长Fred Attakuma、首席执行官Ken Ashigbey博士、行业领袖、传统首领和媒体人士出席了会议。

Tandoh先生在法律问题上态度明确。根据经修订的《2006年矿产与采矿法》（第703号法案），小规模采矿许可证仅保留给加纳公民。他说：“这意味着，任何从事小规模采矿的外国人都构成犯罪。处罚包括20年至25年监禁，并在服刑后驱逐出境。”

他说，该法律还针对“挂名经营”，即外国实体利用加纳人获取矿产权利的行为，并透露，在针对比里姆河和塔诺河等主要河流开展的突击行动中，已有多名中国公民被捕。尽管发出警告，Tandoh先生仍称赞中国对加纳大型采矿业的投资，称其帮助加纳成为非洲最大的黄金生产国和全球第六大黄金生产国。他列举了紫金、赤峰和山东等中国大型矿业企业，并指出，一年前取得阿基姆矿所有权控的紫金，在没有扩大员工队伍或升级基础设施的情况下将产量提高了20%。他还表示，Shandong Gold在加纳的业务是山东集团全球表现最佳的矿山。

他说，中加矿业协会为双方围绕负责任投资、监管合规和可持续发展开展对话提供了制度化平台。他说：“这是为了确保我们在维护双边关系诚信的同时，也维护监管体系的可信度，为我们矿业社区的未来提供保障。”

第一，将中国公民非法采矿作为双边联合执法优先事项，并立即落实2026年中国矿业会议达成的框架。根据该框架，违法者不仅将在加纳受到制裁，中国当局也会通过自身机制对境外公民进行监管。他说：“这条双重执法路径必须立即落实，使驱逐出境不是从轻处理的终点，而是追究责任的前奏。”

第二，中国应与加纳合作，打击为非法采矿提供便利的融资和物流网络。他指出，非法采矿活动组织严密、拥有资金并配备齐全，其设备、资本和供应链有时来自加纳境外。

第三，应将中加矿业协会打造为合规平台，而不只是商业平台；该协会应积极劝阻并举报其成员以及在加纳经营的中国公民的违法行为。他说：“负责任的协会不会庇护违法者，而是会揭露他们。”

Tandoh先生说，矿产委员会将继续不惧压力、不偏不倚地执行法律，同时与认同其透明、可持续矿业愿景的投资者合作。他说：“加纳 deeply珍视中国的友谊，绝不能让少数不法分子的行为破坏这份友谊。中国作为负责任全球投资者的声誉也极其珍贵，不能因那些违法经营者的行为而蒙受玷污。”

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/sena.body: ABUJA – The Senate has passed a bill seeking to strengthen the regulatory oversight of major financial technology companies and other non-bank financial institutions in Nigeria. The proposed legislation will empower the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to designate qualifying financial technology operators and other non-bank institutions as Systemically Important Institutions (SIIs), subjecting them to enhanced regulatory supervision. The bill, SB.959, titled A Bill for an Act to Amend the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act, No. 5 of 2020, to Provide for the Designation, Registration and Enhanced Supervision of Systemically Important Institutions; and for Other Related Matters, was passed on Tuesday after clause-by-clause consideration at the Committee of the Whole. Its passage followed the presentation of a report by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Banking, Insurance and Other Financial Institutions, Senator Adetokunbo Abiru (APC, Lagos East). Under the proposed amendment, the CBN will be empowered to identify and designate non-bank financial institutions as systemically important based on factors such as their size, transaction volumes, customer base and interconnectedness with the wider financial system. The legislation also provides for the establishment of an official register of designated institutions and enhanced prudential supervision to address potential risks to Nigeria’s financial stability. It seeks to subject major fintech operators and other qualifying institutions to stricter requirements on regulatory compliance, corporate governance, cybersecurity, technology-risk management and operational resilience. Other key provisions include stress testing, data-integrity assessments, enhanced regulatory reporting and supervisory access to relevant information and operational systems of designated institutions. The bill also seeks to strengthen beneficial ownership disclosure, improve transparency in ownership and control structures, and establish enforcement mechanisms and sanctions for institutions that violate regulatory requirements. Presenting the committee’s report, Abiru said the proposed amendment was designed to address emerging vulnerabilities in Nigeria’s financial services sector, particularly the growing influence of large technology-driven financial service providers whose operations had become increasingly interconnected with traditional banking institutions. He said the legislation would strengthen the CBN’s capacity to monitor risks arising from digital financial services, technological disruptions and operational failures that could have wider implications for the financial system. Abiru disclosed that the proposed amendment received broad support from regulatory authorities, government agencies, financial institutions and professional bodies during a public hearing conducted on March 4, 2026. According to the committee’s report, the CBN supported the proposed strengthening of the statutory framework for supervising systemically important non-bank financial institutions, particularly large fintech operators whose transaction volumes, customer bases and interconnected operations could affect financial stability. The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) also supported stronger oversight but called for a clear distinction between prudential regulation, competition enforcement and consumer protection. The commission urged coordination between the CBN and FCCPC to avoid duplication of regulatory responsibilities and ensure that the proposed framework promotes fair competition while protecting consumers. Other institutions that supported the bill included the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC), Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), Ministry of Finance Incorporated, Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, Bank of Industry and Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Several banks and other financial institutions also endorsed the proposed amendment. The committee said stakeholders generally supported measures to strengthen financial stability, encourage responsible digital innovation, improve regulatory coordination, promote operational compliance and protect users of financial services. It added that a stakeholder-inclusive legislative approach was adopted to ensure that the proposed amendment reflected the concerns and recommendations of relevant institutions and members of the public. The committee disclosed that the public hearing was preceded by advertisements in print and electronic media inviting memoranda from stakeholders and other interested members of the public. The hearing was declared open on behalf of the President of the Senate by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno (APC, Borno North). The bill had earlier passed second reading on Thursday, December 4, 2025, before being referred to the Senate Committee on Banking, Insurance and Other Financial Institutions for further legislative consideration. The proposed amendment comes amid the rapid expansion of digital financial services in Nigeria, with fintech operators playing increasingly significant roles in payments, electronic transfers and other financial transactions. The legislation seeks to ensure that the growing influence of major non-bank financial institutions is matched by regulatory oversight capable of addressing risks to the wider financial system. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/sena.title_zh: 参议院通过法案，加强尼日利亚中央银行对金融科技企业的监管
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/sena.body_zh: 阿布贾——尼日利亚参议院通过一项法案，旨在加强对大型金融科技公司和其他非银行金融机构的监管。拟议法案将授权尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）指定符合条件的金融科技运营商和其他非银行机构为系统重要性金融机构（SIIs），并使其接受更为严格的监管监督。法案编号为SB.959，题为《一项旨在修订2020年第5号《银行及其他金融机构法》、规定系统重要性金融机构的指定、登记和加强监督及其他相关事项的法案》，于周二在全体委员会逐条审议后获得通过。此前，参议院银行、保险及其他金融机构委员会主席阿德托昆博·阿比鲁参议员（APC，拉各斯东部）提交了委员会报告。根据拟议修正案，CBN将有权根据非银行金融机构的规模、交易量、客户基础及其与更广泛金融体系的互联程度等因素，认定并指定其为系统重要机构。该立法还将建立指定机构的官方登记册，并加强审慎监管，以应对可能对尼日利亚金融稳定造成的风险。法案拟让大型金融科技运营商和其他符合条件的机构在监管合规、公司治理、网络安全、技术风险管理及运营韧性方面遵守更严格的要求。其他关键条款包括压力测试、数据完整性评估、加强监管报告，以及监管机构查阅指定机构相关信息和运营系统的权限。法案还拟加强受益所有权披露，提高所有权和控制结构的透明度，并为违反监管要求的机构设立执法机制和制裁措施。阿比鲁在提交委员会报告时表示，拟议修正案旨在应对尼日利亚金融服务领域新出现的脆弱性，尤其是大型技术驱动型金融服务提供商影响力日益增强的问题，这些机构的业务与传统银行机构之间的互联程度不断上升。他说，该立法将增强CBN监测数字金融服务、技术颠覆和运营失败所引发风险的能力，因为这些问题可能对整个金融体系产生更广泛影响。阿比鲁透露，在2026年3月4日举行的公开听证会上，拟议修正案得到了监管机构、政府部门、金融机构和专业团体的广泛支持。根据委员会报告，CBN支持加强监管系统重要非银行金融机构的法定框架，尤其是支持对大型金融科技运营商实施监管，因为这些机构，其交易量、客户基础和互联业务可能影响金融稳定。联邦竞争与消费者保护委员会（FCCPC）也支持加强监督，但呼吁明确区分审慎监管、竞争执法和消费者保护。该委员会敦促CBN与FCCPC加强协调，避免监管职责重复，并确保拟议框架在保护消费者的同时促进公平竞争。支持该法案的其他机构包括尼日利亚存款保险公司（NDIC）、尼日利亚通信委员会（NCC）、财政部注册机构、联邦工业、贸易与投资部、工业银行以及经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）。多家银行和其他金融机构也支持拟议修正案。委员会表示，利益相关方普遍支持旨在加强金融稳定、鼓励负责任的数字创新、改善监管协调、促进运营合规以及保护金融服务用户的措施。委员会补充称，立法采取了吸纳利益相关方的做法，以确保拟议修正案反映相关机构和公众的意见与建议。委员会透露，公开听证会之前，委员会曾在纸质和电子媒体刊登公告，邀请利益相关方及其他 interested members of the public提交备忘录。参议院党鞭穆罕默德· Tahir·蒙古诺参议员（APC，博尔诺北部）代表参议院议长宣布听证会开幕。该法案此前于2025年12月4日星期四通过二读，随后被提交参议院银行、保险及其他金融机构委员会作进一步立法审议。拟议修正案出台之际，尼日利亚数字金融服务正快速扩张，金融科技运营商在支付、电子转账及其他金融交易中发挥着日益重要的作用。该立法旨在确保主要非银行金融机构日益增强的影响力能够与相应的监管相匹配，以应对整个金融体系面临的风险。本文所表达的意见不代表Vanguard报及其任何员工的观点……

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/s.summary: The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Banking, Insurance and Other Financial Institutions, Senator Mukhail Adetokunbo Abiru, presented the committee’s report on the bill during plenary presided over by Senate President Godswill Akpabio.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/s.summary_zh: 参议院银行、保险及其他金融机构委员会主席穆凯尔·阿德托昆博·阿比鲁参议员，在参议院议长戈德斯维尔·阿克帕比奥主持的全会上提交了该委员会关于相关法案的报告。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/s.body: The Senate on Tuesday, passed for third reading, a bill meant to strengthen the regulatory oversight of Nigeria’s rapidly expanding financial technology sector. The proposed amendment to the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA) seeks to empower the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to designate and regulate systemically important fintech companies and other non-bank financial institutions. The proposed legislation is designed to bring financial institutions whose size, transaction volumes, customer base and operational interconnectedness could pose risks to the country’s financial stability under enhanced regulatory supervision. The initiative, which seeks to amend the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act, 2020, also provides for stricter corporate governance standards, cybersecurity safeguards, technology-risk management, operational resilience and greater transparency in the ownership structures of designated institutions. The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Banking, Insurance and Other Financial Institutions, Senator Mukhail Adetokunbo Abiru, presented the committee’s report on the bill during plenary presided over by Senate President Godswill Akpabio. The bill, SB. 959, is titled: A Bill for an Act to Amend the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act, No. 5 of 2020, to Provide for the Designation, Registration and Enhanced Supervision of Systemically Important Institutions; and for Other Related Matters. Abiru, who represents Lagos East Senatorial District, sponsored the legislation alongside members of the Senate Committee on Banking, Insurance and Other Financial Institutions. The proposed amendment seeks to address emerging vulnerabilities in Nigeria’s financial services industry, particularly the growing influence of large technology-driven financial service providers whose operations have become increasingly interconnected with the traditional banking system. Under the proposed framework, the CBN would be empowered to identify and designate qualifying non-bank financial institutions as Systemically Important Institutions (SIIs), subjecting them to enhanced prudential supervision. The proposed legislation also seeks to establish clear criteria and regulatory procedures for determining which institutions qualify for the designation. Beyond conventional financial regulation, the bill seeks to strengthen the capacity of the CBN to monitor risks arising from digital financial services, technological disruptions and operational failures that could have wider implications for the financial system. Among its key provisions are stress testing, data-integrity assessments, enhanced regulatory reporting and supervisory access to relevant information and operational systems of designated institutions. It also seeks to strengthen beneficial ownership disclosure and regulatory oversight of ownership and control structures, while providing enforcement mechanisms and sanctions for institutions that violate applicable regulatory requirements. The committee’s report disclosed that the proposed legislation received broad support from relevant regulatory authorities, government agencies, financial institutions and professional bodies during a public hearing conducted on March 4, 2026. The CBN supported the proposed strengthening of the statutory framework for supervising systemically important non-bank financial institutions. The apex bank specifically highlighted the need for effective, risk-based supervision of large fintech operators, noting that their transaction volumes, customer bases and operational interconnectedness could have significant implications for financial stability. The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) also supported stronger oversight of systemically important financial service providers but emphasised the need to maintain a clear distinction between prudential regulation, competition enforcement and consumer protection. The commission urged appropriate coordination between the CBN and the FCCPC to prevent duplication of regulatory responsibilities and ensure that the proposed framework promotes fair competition while protecting consumers. Other institutions that supported the bill included the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC), Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), Ministry of Finance Incorporated, Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, Bank of Industry and Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Several banks and other financial institutions also endorsed the proposed amendment. According to the committee, the submissions received from stakeholders generally supported the need to strengthen financial stability, encourage responsible digital innovation, improve regulatory coordination, promote operational compliance and protect users of financial services. The committee explained that it had adopted a stakeholder-inclusive legislative approach to ensure that the proposed amendment reflected the concerns and recommendations of relevant institutions and members of the public. It said the public hearing was preceded by advertisements in print and electronic media inviting memoranda from stakeholders and other interested members of the public. The public hearing was declared open on behalf of the President of the Senate by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Munguno. The committee recalled that the Senate had passed the bill through second reading on Thursday, December 4, 2025, before referring it to the Committee on Banking, Insurance and Other Financial Institutions for further legislative consideration. The proposed amendment comes against the backdrop of the rapid expansion of digital financial services in Nigeria, with fintech operators playing increasingly significant roles in payments, transfers and other financial transactions. The proposed regulatory framework is expected to address potential systemic vulnerabilities by ensuring that institutions whose operations could affect the wider financial system are subjected to appropriate supervision, regardless of whether they operate as conventional banks. It also seeks to promote regulatory accountability through the establishment of an official register of designated Systemically Important Institutions. The proposed legislation further underscores the importance of ensuring that technological innovation in the financial services industry does not undermine financial stability, consumer confidence and the integrity of the country’s financial system. The Senate after the clause-by-clause consideration of the report at the Committee of the whole, subsequently passed the proposed legislation for third reading at plenary. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/s.title_zh: 参议院通过法案，将大型金融科技企业和非银行金融机构纳入尼日利亚中央银行监管
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/10/s.body_zh: 参议院周二通过一项法案的第三次审议，该法案旨在加强对尼日利亚快速扩张的金融科技行业的监管。对《银行及其他金融机构法》（BOFIA）的拟议修正案拟赋予尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）认定并监管系统重要性金融科技公司及其他非银行金融机构的权力。拟议立法旨在将那些规模、交易量、客户群和运营互联程度可能对尼日利亚金融稳定构成风险的金融机构纳入加强监管监督之下。这项拟议修正案除寻求修订2020年《银行及其他金融机构法》外，还将规定更严格的公司治理标准、网络安全防护措施、技术风险管理、运营韧性，以及提高指定机构所有权结构的透明度。参议院银行、保险及其他金融机构委员会主席穆凯尔·阿德托昆博·阿比鲁参议员在参议院议长戈茨维尔·阿卡皮奥主持的全会上提交了委员会关于该法案的报告。该法案编号为SB. 959，题为：《一项旨在修订2020年第5号《银行及其他金融机构法》、规定系统重要性机构的认定、登记和加强监督以及其他相关事项的法案》。阿比鲁代表拉各斯东选区，与参议院银行、保险及其他金融机构委员会成员共同提案。该拟议修正案旨在应对尼日利亚金融服务行业新出现的脆弱性，尤其是大型科技驱动型金融服务提供商影响力日益扩大的问题，这些机构的业务与传统银行体系的互联程度不断加深。根据拟议框架，尼日利亚中央银行将有权认定符合条件的非银行金融机构为系统重要性机构（SIIs），并使其接受加强的审慎监管。拟议立法还将制定明确标准和监管程序，以确定哪些机构符合认定资格。法案除涉及传统金融监管外，还旨在加强尼日利亚中央银行监测数字金融服务、技术颠覆和运营故障所引发风险的能力，因为这些风险可能对整个金融体系产生更广泛影响。其主要条款包括压力测试、数据完整性评估、加强监管报告，以及监管机构查阅指定机构相关信息和运营系统的权限。法案还将加强实际受益所有权披露，以及对所有权和控制结构的监管监督，同时为违反适用监管要求的机构规定执法机制和制裁措施。委员会的报告披露，在2026年3月4日举行的公开听证会上，相关监管机构、政府部门、金融机构和专业团体普遍支持该拟议立法。尼日利亚中央银行支持加强监督系统重要性非银行金融机构的法定框架。该最高银行机构特别强调，有必要对大型金融科技运营商实施有效的、基于风险的监管，并指出其交易量、客户群和运营互联程度可能对金融稳定产生重大影响。联邦竞争与消费者保护委员会（FCCPC）也支持加强对系统重要性金融服务提供商的监督，但强调需要明确区分审慎监管、竞争执法和消费者保护。该委员会敦促尼日利亚中央银行与联邦竞争与消费者保护委员会适当协调，防止监管职责重复，并确保拟议框架在保护消费者的同时促进公平竞争。支持该法案的其他机构还包括尼日利亚存款保险公司（NDIC）、尼日利亚通信委员会（NCC）、财政部公司、联邦工业、贸易与投资部、工业银行以及经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）。多家银行及其他金融机构也支持该拟议修正案。委员会表示，相关利益攸关方提交的意见总体支持加强金融稳定、鼓励负责任的数字创新、改善监管协调、促进运营合规以及保护金融服务用户的需要。委员会解释称，其采用了利益攸关方参与的立法方式，以确保拟议修正案反映相关机构和公众的关切与建议。委员会表示，公开听证会前，委员会通过纸质和电子媒体发布广告，邀请利益攸关方及其他关注公共事务的人士提交意见书。参议院党鞭穆罕默德·塔希尔·蒙古诺参议员代表参议院议长宣布公开听证会开幕。委员会回顾称，参议院已于2025年12月4日星期四通过该法案的第二次审议，随后将其提交银行、保险及其他金融机构委员会作进一步立法审议。拟议修正案出台的背景是尼日利亚数字金融服务迅速扩张，金融科技运营商在支付、转账及其他金融交易中发挥着日益重要的作用。预计拟议监管框架将通过确保可能影响整个金融体系的机构接受适当监督来应对潜在的系统性脆弱性，无论这些机构以传统银行形式运营。法案还将通过建立系统重要性机构官方登记册来促进监管问责。拟议立法进一步强调，必须确保金融服务行业的技术创新不会削弱金融稳定、消费者信心及尼日利亚金融体系的完整性。参议院在全院委员会逐条审议报告后，随后在全体会议上通过该拟议立法的第三次审议。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY https://www.thegazellenews.com/abuja-nuj.body: The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Council, has won a Gold Medal at the 8th Nigeria-China Table Tennis Friendship Tournament 2026, reinforcing the role of sports in promoting international friendship and cultural exchange. The tournament, held on Sunday at the China Cultural Centre in Abuja, brought together Nigerian and Chinese participants to promote bilateral relations, cultural understanding and people-to-people engagement through sports. The Chairman of NUJ FCT Council, Comrade Grace Ike, described the competition as an opportunity for journalists to connect beyond newsroom activities while promoting physical fitness, discipline, teamwork and professional solidarity. Ike commended the China Cultural Centre for sustaining its partnership with the NUJ FCT Council over the eight editions of the tournament, saying the initiative had strengthened cultural understanding and people-to-people relations between Nigeria and China. She said that beyond the prizes and competitive excitement, the tournament’s greatest value lay in the friendship, unity and partnerships it continued to foster among participants. She congratulated the winners and other participants, urging them to uphold mutual respect, compassion and unity alongside the competitive spirit of sports. Earlier, the Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria, Mr Yang Jianxing, described the tournament as an important platform for promoting mutual understanding, trust and friendship between Nigerians and Chinese. He said exchanges and handshakes on the table tennis court reflected mutual respect, teamwork and fair play, adding that sports could transcend language and cultural differences to build lasting relationships. Yang commended the NUJ and the Nigerian media for their contributions to objective reporting of developments in Nigeria-China relations, particularly in trade, investment, culture, education, science and technology. He said the media played an important role in strengthening mutual understanding, promoting cultural exchanges and deepening relations between the two countries. The Chinese diplomat also acknowledged the contributions of the Nigerian-China Chamber of Commerce and Chinese enterprises operating in Nigeria to economic cooperation, trade, investment and people-to-people exchanges. He noted that 2026 marked the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges and the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Nigeria and China. Yang also highlighted China’s decision to extend zero-tariff treatment, effective May 1, 2026, to imports from 53 African countries with which it maintains diplomatic relations. He expressed hope that the tournament would further strengthen cooperation among the sporting, media and business communities and contribute to closer Nigeria-China relations. In the men’s singles category, Mr Ignatius Nkwoh of the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) emerged champion, winning the Gold Medal. Nkwoh expressed appreciation to God, the NUJ FCT Council leadership and the organisers for providing the opportunity to participate in the competition. He dedicated his trophy to Ike and members of the council’s executive for their encouragement and commitment to promoting sporting activities among journalists. Other NUJ FCT Council participants also recorded notable performances, including a Bronze Medal in the mixed doubles category and a third-place finish in the men’s singles event. The tournament underscored the role of sports in fostering diplomacy, cultural understanding and international cooperation, while reaffirming the longstanding friendship between Nigeria and China. The NUJ FCT Council appreciated the sponsors, partners, participants and organisers for the successful eighth edition and expressed optimism about an even more impactful ninth edition in 2027
https://www.thegazellenews.com/abuja-nuj.title_zh: 阿布贾尼日利亚记者协会在第八届尼日利亚—中国乒乓球友谊赛中夺得金牌
https://www.thegazellenews.com/abuja-nuj.body_zh: 尼日利亚记者协会联邦首都 territory委员会在2026年第八届尼日利亚—中国乒乓球友谊赛中夺得金牌，进一步体现了体育在促进国际友谊和文化交流方面的作用。赛事于周日在阿布贾中国文化中心举行，汇聚尼日利亚和中国参赛者，通过体育推动双边关系、文化理解和民间交流。尼日利亚记者协会联邦首都territory委员会主席格雷丝·伊克同志表示，这项比赛让记者有机会在新闻编辑室工作之外加强联系，同时促进身体素质、纪律、团队合作和职业团结。伊克称赞中国文化中心在连续八届赛事中与尼日利亚记者协会联邦首都territory委员会保持合作，并表示，这一举措加强了尼日利亚与中国之间的文化理解和民间关系。她说，除了奖品和竞技带来的兴奋之外，这项赛事最大的价值在于持续促成参赛者之间的友谊、团结和合作。她祝贺获奖者及其他参赛者，敦促他们在竞技精神之外恪守相互尊重、慈悲和团结。此前，中国驻尼日利亚大使馆参赞杨建兴表示，这项赛事是促进尼日利亚人与中国人相互理解、信任和友谊的重要平台。他说，乒乓球赛场上的交流和握手体现了相互尊重、团队合作和公平竞赛精神，并指出体育能够跨越语言和文化差异，建立持久的关系。杨赞扬尼日利亚记者协会和尼日利亚媒体为客观报道尼日利亚—中国关系各领域发展所作的贡献，特别是贸易、投资、文化、教育、科学技术等方面。他表示，媒体在加强相互理解、促进文化交流以及深化两国关系方面发挥了重要作用。这位中国外交官还肯定了尼日利亚—中国商会以及在尼日利亚经营的中国企业为经济合作、贸易、投资和民间交流作出的贡献。他指出，2026年是中非民间交流年，也是尼日利亚与中国建交55周年。杨还强调，中国决定自2026年5月1日起，将零关税待遇扩大至从与其保持外交关系的53个非洲国家进口的商品。他希望本次赛事进一步加强体育、媒体和商业社群之间的合作，推动尼日利亚—中国关系更加紧密。在男子单打项目中，尼日利亚电视局（NTA）的伊格内修斯·恩克沃先生夺得冠军，获得金牌。恩克沃感谢上帝、尼日利亚记者协会联邦首都territory委员会领导层以及赛事组织者为参赛提供的机会。他将奖杯献给伊克和委员会执行成员，感谢他们的鼓励以及推动记者体育活动的投入。尼日利亚记者协会联邦首都territory委员会的其他参赛者也取得了令人瞩目的成绩，包括在混合双打项目中获得铜牌，以及在男子单打项目中获得第三名。这项赛事凸显了体育在推动外交、文化理解和国际合作方面的作用，同时再次确认了尼日利亚与中国之间的长期友谊。尼日利亚记者协会联邦首都territory委员会感谢赞助商、合作伙伴、参赛者和组织者共同办好第八届赛事，并乐观期待2027年第九届赛事产生更大的影响力

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/fina.body: Layer 1 . –1,000 business leaders to sign pact on policy reforms, enterprise growth at Blueprint Summit 2.0 December 3 As Gaye seeks 50-year African businesses, unveils digital platform ABUJA –THE Presidency on Tuesday, said Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy by 2030 depends largely on bringing millions of economically active Nigerians, particularly women, youths and small business owners, into the formal financial system. The Presidency also noted that to unlock the $1 trillion future by 2030, Nigeria must urgently formalize its grassroots economy, maintaining that bringing millions of women, youth, and small business owners into the formal financial system is no longer optional but a prerequisite for growth. Technical Adviser to the President on Economic and Financial Inclusion, Dr Nurudeen Abubakar Zauro, stated this in Abuja while announcing a partnership between the Presidential Committee on Economic and Financial Inclusion (PreCEFI) and the Africa CEO Club ahead of the Africa Blueprint Summit 2.0 billed to hold on December 3, 2026. Zauro said financial inclusion must go beyond opening bank accounts to providing individuals and businesses with access to credit, savings, insurance, pensions, investment opportunities and wider markets. He maintained that the Federal Government’s economic transformation agenda could not achieve its full potential while significant segments of the population remained excluded from formal financial services and productive economic activities. According to him, financial inclusion is a critical driver of economic growth, enterprise development, job creation and national prosperity. According to him: “This work sits at the heart of the Federal Government’s economic agenda. Millions of our citizens, many of them women, young people, rural households and small business owners, still operate outside the formal financial system. ”They lack access to savings, credit, insurance and pensions. If we are to build a one trillion dollar economy, we cannot leave them behind. Inclusion is not charity. It is growth.” The presidential aide said PreCEFI, under the leadership of Vice President Kashim Shettima, was coordinating government institutions, regulators and private-sector stakeholders to expand financial access and ensure that no economically active Nigerian was left behind. Zauro identified digital public infrastructure, consumer protection and simplified onboarding procedures as essential to removing barriers to financial services, particularly the challenges of formal identification and inadequate banking facilities. He stressed that financial inclusion must translate into productive activities, including business expansion, agricultural financing, employment generation and access to domestic and international markets. ”Opening an account is the first step, not the last. True inclusion means that the small business can borrow, grow, hire and one day sell across borders,” he said. Explaining the partnership with Africa CEO Club, Zauro said the collaboration would bridge the gap between financial inclusion and enterprise development by connecting entrepreneurs with institutions offering finance, regulatory support and market opportunities. The summit themed “The Builders’ Mandate: From Blueprint to Build,” is scheduled for December 3, 2026, at the Congress Hall of Transcorp Hilton, Abuja, with about 1,000 business leaders, investors, policymakers and regulators expected from across Africa and the diaspora. He said participants would develop a Builders’ Mandate outlining 10 priority policy interventions expected from governments and 10 corresponding commitments from the private sector to promote economic growth, investment and sustainable businesses. Zauro said PreCEFI would ensure that the interests of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), particularly women, and youth-led businesses, feature prominently in discussions on access to capital, regulatory reforms and enterprise development. In her remarks, President of the Africa CEO Club, Dr Fatoumatta Gaye, said the summit would address what she described as Africa’s “institutional deficit”, characterised by the inability of many businesses to survive beyond their founders. She lamented that several African enterprises lacked effective succession plans, management structures and institutional frameworks to ensure continuity across generations. ”Africa does not lack brilliant founders. What we lack are institutions that outlive them. Too many of our businesses rise with one person and fall with that same person. Too few become 50-year companies,” she said. Gaye said the Builders’ Mandate would be endorsed by participating business leaders and presented to governments, while the Africa CEO Club would monitor and publicly report progress on its implementation throughout 2027. She recalled that the maiden edition, held on November 27, 2025, at the Afreximbank African Trade Centre, Abuja, attracted more than 600 business and policy leaders and over 60 media organisations. She disclosed that the inaugural summit facilitated business transactions through its Deal Room and secured $5 million for the development of the Africa CEO Club’s digital ecosystem. According to her, the organisation has since established its headquarters in Abuja, recruited more than 60 employees, expanded its membership and strengthened partnerships with public- and private-sector institutions. She said the digital platform, designed to connect business leaders and enterprises across Africa, would be launched on March 18, 2027. On the December summit, Gaye said the first panel, “Capital That Builds,” would examine sustainable financing and long-term capital for business expansion. Expected speakers, she said, include AMCON Managing Director, Gbenga Alade; Managing Director of the Bank of Agriculture, Ayo Sotinrin; Moniepoint Chief Executive Officer, Tosin Eniolorunda; and Director-General of the Governance Delivery Unit, Dr Olusiji Aina. Other sessions will address policy as infrastructure, business succession and institutional development, alongside a founders’ conversation, live podcast, investment Deal Room and exhibition for MSMEs and start-ups seeking investors, buyers and development partners. Gaye said the event would also be livestreamed to an expected audience of at least three million people. Describing the partnership with PreCEFI as strategic, Gaye said financial inclusion was fundamental to building sustainable enterprises, citing women traders seeking their first bank accounts, young entrepreneurs accessing loans and small manufacturers entering export markets. She urged African business owners and investors to participate in the summit, arguing that collective engagement would strengthen the private sector’s influence on policies concerning taxation, access to finance and investment. Gaye announced that early-bird registration would close on November 15, while groups registering more than three participants would receive a 20 per cent discount. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/fina.title_zh: 金融普惠是蒂努布实现1万亿美元国内生产总值目标的关键
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/fina.body_zh: 第一层。Blueprint Summit 2.0将于12月3日举行，1,000名商界领袖将签署有关政策改革和企业发展的协议；Gaye寻求打造可存续50年的非洲企业，并公布数字平台。阿布贾——总统府周二表示，尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）力争到2030年建成1万亿美元经济，其目标在很大程度上取决于能否让数百万经济活跃的尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）民众，尤其是女性、青年和小企业主，正式纳入金融体系。总统府还指出，要释放尼日利亚到2030年实现1万亿美元经济前景的潜力，尼日利亚必须 urgently 推动基层经济正规化，并强调让数百万女性、青年和小企业主正式纳入金融体系已不再是可选项，而是增长的必要前提。总统经济与金融包容技术顾问Dr Nurudeen Abubakar Zauro周二在阿布贾宣布了总统经济与金融包容委员会（PreCEFI）与Africa CEO Club的合作，同时宣布将于2026年12月3日举行的Africa Blueprint Summit 2.0。Zauro表示，金融包容必须超越开设银行账户，进一步为个人和企业提供信贷、储蓄、保险、养老金、投资机会以及进入更广泛市场的渠道。他强调，在population中仍有相当一部分人被排除在正规金融服务和生产性经济活动之外的情况下，联邦政府的经济转型议程无法充分发挥潜力。据他所说，金融包容是经济增长、企业发展、创造就业和国家繁荣的重要驱动力。他表示：“这项工作处于联邦政府经济议程的核心位置。数百万公民仍游离于正规金融体系之外，其中许多是女性、年轻人、农村家庭和小企业主。他们无法获得储蓄、信贷、保险和养老金。如果我们要建设一个1万亿美元的经济体，就不能把他们落下。包容不是施舍，而是增长。”总统助理表示，在副总统Kashim Shettima的领导下，PreCEFI正协调政府机构、监管部门和私营部门利益相关方，以扩大金融可及性，确保没有任何经济活跃的尼日利亚人掉队。Zauro指出，数字公共基础设施、消费者保护和简化的开户程序，是消除金融服务障碍的关键，尤其是正式身份认证困难和银行设施不足等问题。他强调，金融包容必须转化为生产性活动，包括扩大经营、农业融资、创造就业以及进入国内和国际市场。“开户是第一步，而不是最后一步。真正的包容意味着小企业能够借贷、发展、招聘，并最终跨境销售，”他说。Zauro在解释与Africa CEO Club的合作时表示，双方将通过把创业者与提供融资、监管支持和市场机会的机构连接起来，弥合金融包容与企业发展之间的鸿沟。峰会主题为“建设者的使命：从蓝图走向建设”，定于2026年12月3日在阿布贾Transcorp Hilton的Congress Hall举行，预计将有约1,000名来自非洲各地及非洲侨民的商业领袖、投资者、政策制定者和监管人员参加。他说，与会者将制定一项“建设者的使命”，提出政府对政策落实的10项优先干预措施，以及私营部门为促进经济增长、投资和可持续发展的 Businesses 所需的10项相应承诺。Zauro表示，PreCEFI将确保微型、小型和中型企业（MSMEs），尤其是女性企业和青年主导企业，在资本获取、监管改革和企业发展等讨论中得到充分重视。Africa CEO Club主席Dr Fatoumatta Gaye在发言中说，本次峰会将探讨她所称的非洲“制度赤字”，其特征是许多企业无法在创始人之后继续生存。她哀叹，非洲许多企业缺乏有效的继任计划、管理架构和确保跨代延续的制度框架。“非洲不缺杰出的创始人。我们缺的是能够比他们存续更久的制度。我们的太多企业随一个人崛起，又随同一个人衰败。能够成为50年企业的太少，”她说。Gaye表示，“建设者的使命”将由参会商业领袖签署并提交给各国政府，Africa CEO Club则将在整个2027年监督执行情况并公开报告进展。她回顾说，首届峰会于2025年11月27日在阿布贾Afreximbank African Trade Centre举行，吸引了600多名商业和政策领袖以及60多家媒体机构。她透露，首届峰会通过其Deal Room促成商业交易，并为Africa CEO Club数字生态系统的发展筹集了500万美元。据她说，该组织此后已在阿布贾设立总部，招聘了60多名员工，扩大了会员规模，并加强了与公共部门和私营部门机构的合作。她说，旨在连接非洲各地商业领袖和企业的数字平台将于2027年3月18日上线。关于12月举行的峰会，Gaye表示，首场论坛“建设资本”将探讨企业扩张所需的可持续融资和长期资本。她说，预计发言者包括AMCON董事总经理Gbenga Alade、农业银行董事总经理Ayo Sotinrin、Moniepoint首席执行官Tosin Eniolorunda，以及Governance Delivery Unit总干事Dr Olusiji Aina。其他场次将讨论政策作为基础设施、企业继任和制度发展，并包括创始人对话、现场播客、投资Deal Room，以及面向寻求投资者、买家和发展伙伴的MSMEs和初创企业的展览。Gaye表示，活动还将直播，预计观众至少达到300万人。Gaye在描述与PreCEFI的合作时称其具有战略意义，并表示金融包容是建设可持续企业的基础。她以寻求首个银行账户的女性商人、获得贷款以扩大经营的年轻创业者，以及进入出口市场的小型制造商为例，敦促非洲企业主和投资者参加峰会，认为各方共同参与将增强私营部门在税收、融资渠道和投资等政策问题上的影响力。Gaye宣布，早鸟注册将于11月15日截止；团体注册超过3名参与者可享受20%的折扣。本文表达的意见不代表Vanguard newspapers及其任何员工的观点

READ: WPS: PH upbeat on progress in South China Sea code of conduct talks Asked whether the COC would be settled during the Asean Summit scheduled for Nov. 15 to 17, Castro said, “Alam naman natin na isa ito sa nais ng Pangulo na ma-finalize.” (We know that this is one of the things the president wants to finalize.) Castro said Marcos remains hopeful about reaching an agreement, even as the Philippines nears the end of its hosting of the Asean Summit. “Ang nais ng Pangulo ay magandang makikipagrelasyon sa lahat ng bansa at kung anuman ang maaaring maging agreement para sa kapayapaan ng rehiyon, iyon ang nais ng Pangulo,” she said. The proposed Code of Conduct is intended to establish rules governing the behavior of countries in the disputed waters and prevent incidents that could lead to armed conflict. Asean and China adopted the nonbinding Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea in 2002, but negotiations for a more comprehensive agreement have continued for decades. In a media interview in October, Marcos noted “good progress” in the negotiations for the COC in the South China Sea. “We’re working very, very hard, we’re making good progress as a matter of fact, in terms of the code of conduct,” Marcos told Forbes Chair and editor-in-chief Steve Forbes during an onstage discussion at the 24th Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore. “The discussions have been going on for a while, and sometimes it’s a bit frustrating that just the definitions of ordinary words are becoming bones of contention,” he said. “But we are determined to come to an agreement and to hopefully de-escalate the situation,” he added. The warning was issued by the department’s Bureau of Consular Affairs in a post on its official Facebook page on Monday, citing security concerns, prevailing local conditions and the US government’s limited capacity to provide assistance to its citizens in the affected countries. Explaining the classification, the department said Level 4 advisories were reserved for destinations considered dangerous, urging Americans to avoid travelling to the countries regardless of the circumstances. “Level 4 means DO NOT TRAVEL. We assign Level 4 based on local conditions and/or our limited ability to help Americans there. These places are dangerous. Do not go for ANY reason,” the department stated. The US Department of State operates a four-tier travel advisory system to guide American citizens planning international trips. Under the system, Level 1 advises travellers to exercise normal precautions, while Level 2 recommends increased caution because of potential risks. Level 3 urges Americans to reconsider their travel plans, while Level 4 represents the highest warning category, advising against all travel to the designated destinations. The department also urged Americans to consult its official travel advisory website for country-specific security updates and other relevant information before making international travel arrangements. Travellers can access the advisories through its website at travel.state.gov/destination. We’ve got the edge. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: Ambassador Steel calls for 'level playing field' for American firms in Korea The transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) from the United States to South Korea is unlikely to happen during the remaining two years of the Trump administration, former acting U.S. Ambassador to South Korea Joseph Yun said Tuesday. He said there is no consensus in Washington that conditions are met, adding that the same applies to Seoul’s nuclear submarine ambitions and its U.S. investment pledge. “There is no consensus in Washington, for example, that conditions are ready for wartime OPCON to be transferred,” Yun, who also served as the State Department’s special representative for North Korea policy, said during the second Korea-U.S. Diplomatic Forum, which he joined remotely from the U.S. “Conditions are factors. It is never going to be ready but that still remains an issue and I cannot imagine it moving very rapidly,” he added. His remarks came about a week after the U.S. midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of Congress, both House and Senate, and amid differences between the two allies over the timing and conditions of the transfer. South Korea wants to reclaim wartime OPCON by 2028, while the U.S. favors the first quarter of 2029. Yun said the two countries approach the issue differently, and that the Trump administration’s weakening authority in its final two years would make the transfer harder to complete. “The reality is that OPCON transfer is not a political issue in Washington. It is a technical issue,” he said. He also cautioned that regaining OPCON would inevitably reshape the alliance. “South Korean people want to have the OPCON back with no weakening of the alliance. That is impossible. There is no way Koreans can have OPCON back without weakening the alliance structure,” Yun said. “If the Korean capability is so great, a little bit of weakening of the alliance is OK ... But that's a political decision South Korea has to make.” He added, however, that there will be no withdrawal of U.S. troops from South Korea, as their presence enjoys bipartisan support, while stressing that the alliance would remain foundationally sound. Yun expected similarly slow progress on other bilateral negotiations that have been delayed amid friction between the allies, including nuclear and investment issues. “There is no consensus in Washington that Korea ought to have enrichment or nuclear submarines, so those things I find will be very difficult,” he said. Regarding South Korea's investment pledges, he said many Americans are “having trouble fundamentally grasping why there is a commitment for this huge amount of money in certain sectors in the United States,” and that he did not expect it to materialize within the next two years. Yun also ruled out a summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, saying Kim sees nothing to gain. “(Kim) has no interest in meeting with Trump. So I just don't think such a meeting would happen,” Yun said, noting that Pyongyang is no longer isolated, given its backing from Russia and China. The central question, according to Yun, is whether the Trump administration would acknowledge North Korea as a nuclear weapons state — a step he said would draw criticism from Democrats. “Supposing it did happen and Trump has nothing to say on denuclearization, I think the reception from the Democratic Party in the United States will be very poor. He would be heavily criticized, and because really denuclearization of North Korea will remain the central pillar of the U.S. policy, even though a lot of people will acknowledge that this is not something that could happen sooner,” he said. At the same forum, U.S. Ambassador to South Korea Michelle Steel emphasized the alliance’s dual role in security and economics. “Security and prosperity go together. Seventy-six years ago, we fought together to protect the young Republic of Korea. Since then, our economies and culture have become tightly intertwined. We are not only security allies but indispensable economic partners,” she said, adding the Korea-U.S. alliance should grow together. In an apparent reference to the dispute over U.S.-headquartered e-commerce company Coupang, Steel also called for fair treatment of American firms. “Of course, there is always room to do more as our two presidents committed," she said. "American companies in Korea deserve to compete on a level playing field that starts with understanding each other better.”
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title_zh: 前美国外交官称，特朗普任内不太可能完成军事维和行动移交
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh:
Steel大使呼吁为美国企业在韩国营造“公平竞争环境”

美国前驻韩国代理大使约瑟夫·云周二表示，在特朗普政府剩余的两年任期内，美国不太可能将战时作战指挥权（OPCON）移交给韩国。他说，华盛顿尚未就是否具备移交条件达成共识，并指出首尔追求核潜艇及美国投资承诺的问题同样如此。

“例如，华盛顿对于是否已准备好移交战时作战指挥权并没有共识。”云在第二届韩美外交论坛期间说。他曾担任美国国务院对朝政策特别代表，并从美国远程参加论坛。“条件取决于各种因素。准备工作永远不可能完全就绪，但这仍是一个悬而未决的问题，我无法想象推进速度会有多快。”他补充说。

他的这番言论发表在美国中期选举约一周之后。民主党在此次选举中赢得国会参众两院的控制权，而美韩两个盟友对于移交的时间和条件也存有分歧。韩国希望在2028年前收回战时作战指挥权，美国则主张推迟至2029年第一季度。云说，两国看待这一问题的方式不同，而特朗普政府最后两年权威的削弱将使移交更难完成。

“现实情况是，移交作战指挥权在华盛顿并非政治问题，而是技术问题。”他说。他还警告，收回作战指挥权必然重塑美韩同盟关系。

“韩国人民希望在不削弱同盟关系的情况下收回作战指挥权，这是不可能的。韩国人不可能在不让同盟架构 weakened 的情况下收回作战指挥权。”云说，“如果韩方的能力足够强大，同盟关系略微削弱也可以接受……但这是韩国必须作出的政治决定。”不过，他也强调，美国不会从韩国撤军，因为美军驻韩得到两党支持，同时强调同盟关系的根基依然稳固。

云预计，由于美韩之间摩擦不断，包括核问题和投资问题在内的其他双边谈判也不会取得太大进展。“华盛顿对于韩国是否应当拥有核浓缩能力或核潜艇没有共识，因此我认为，这些事情会非常难推进。”他说。

谈及韩国作出的投资承诺，云表示，许多美国人“从根本上难以理解，为何美国某些行业会承诺投入如此巨额资金”，并称他不期待这些承诺能在未来两年内兑现。

云还排除了美国总统唐纳德·特朗普与朝鲜领导人金正恩举行峰会的可能性，称金正恩认为会面没有任何好处。

“（金正恩）没有兴趣与特朗普会面。因此，我认为这种会面不会发生。”云说，并指出，在俄罗斯和中国支持朝鲜的情况下，平壤已不再受到孤立。

据云所述，核心问题是特朗普政府是否愿意承认朝鲜为核武国家。他表示，此举将招致民主党人的批评。

“假设特朗普真的这样做，却对无核化只字不提，我认为美国民主党的反应会非常糟糕。他将受到严厉批评，因为朝鲜无核化仍将是美国政策的核心支柱，尽管许多人会承认这不可能在较短时间内实现。”他说。

在同一场论坛上，美国驻韩国大使米歇尔·steel强调，同盟关系在安全和经济两方面发挥着双重作用。

“安全与繁荣密不可分。76年前，我们并肩作战，保护年轻的大韩民国。此后，我们的经济和文化已紧密交织。我们不仅是安全盟友，也是不可或缺的经济伙伴。”她说，并强调韩美同盟应当共同发展。

显然是在影射围绕美国总部电商企业Coupang的争议，Steel还呼吁为美国企业提供公平待遇。

“当然，正如两国总统所承诺的那样，我们始终还有更多工作要做。”她说，“在韩国的美国企业应当获得公平竞争的环境，而这一切应从更好地相互理解开始。”

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title: 'Honey trap': Nvidia spy scandal puts Korea on alert
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a Chinese woman accused of spying for Beijing has emerged as a significant national security concern for the United States. The scandal erupted amid an intensifying race between the U.S. and China for global leadership in artificial intelligence (AI).
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary_zh: Nvidia首席执行官黄仁勋与一名被控为北京从事间谍活动的中国女子有染一事，已成为美国重大的国家安全关切。这场丑闻爆发之际，美国与中国争夺人工智能全球领导权的竞赛正日益激烈。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a Chinese woman accused of spying for Beijing has emerged as a significant national security concern for the United States. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang, who worked as a business executive at Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed in 2023, allegedly collected intelligence and passed it on to China. The scandal erupted amid an intensifying race between the U.S. and China for global leadership in artificial intelligence (AI). Yoo Seong-ok, a retired intelligence official who previously served as president of the Institute for National Security Strategy during his career at the National Intelligence Service (NIS), warned that South Korea is equally vulnerable to espionage operations by foreign intelligence agencies seeking to steal critical technologies. “Chinese [or] North Korean spies — or both — could have used, or may still be using, a similar honey trap to the one allegedly used against Nvidia CEO Huang to gather confidential information and pass it on to their intelligence agencies,” he told The Korea Times. More significantly, Yoo suggested that sensitive information about Samsung Electronics, SK hynix and their technologies may already have been passed to Chinese rivals, given Nvidia’s close business ties with the two Korean chipmakers. Jensen Huang has held several meetings under what has been dubbed the “AI buddy alliance” with Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong and SK hynix Chairman Chey Tae-won, both in South Korea and the United States. “According to media reports, the Nvidia CEO and Alice Huang are said to have been intimate. He could have unconsciously shared details of his meetings with Korean business leaders when talking to the woman. Who knows?” Yoo said. South Korea has ample reason to be a target of foreign espionage. Its manufacturers play a pivotal role in the global AI industry, supplying the critical components that power AI computing. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix dominate the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) market, together accounting for more than 80 percent of global market share. Their strategic importance to the global AI supply chain makes both companies, as well as their top executives, potential targets of foreign intelligence operations. In recent years, a clear trend has emerged across the global intelligence community: Countries are strengthening their intelligence capabilities to address evolving security challenges. The European Commission is considering establishing an intelligence body under President Ursula von der Leyen to respond to technological and geopolitical challenges in the AI era. Japan has taken similar steps, undertaking a national security and intelligence overhaul since Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi took office. The country has also established a National Intelligence Council to oversee its intelligence strategy. In August, the Defense Counterintelligence Command was disbanded, more than a year after its involvement in former President Yoon Suk Yeol’s Dec. 3, 2024, martial law declaration. The NIS’ counterintelligence capabilities have also been significantly weakened since January 2024, when its authority to detect and investigate espionage cases was transferred to the police. “Since then, not a single North Korean spy has been apprehended. This suggests that the country is doing virtually nothing about counterintelligence,” Yoo said. Jang shared similar concerns. He noted that countries around the world have intensified intelligence gathering and analysis activities to cope with the changing security environment. “Countries such as China, Russia and North Korea have stepped up espionage operations to obtain critical technologies and intelligence. Given this situation, what South Korea has done makes little sense,” he said. Beyond semiconductors, Jang warned that other strategic sectors, particularly the defense industry, are increasingly becoming targets of foreign espionage. He stressed that South Korea must urgently strengthen its counterintelligence capabilities to protect its strategic technologies, industrial assets and national security
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title_zh: “蜜 trap”风波：Nvidia间谍丑闻令韩国提高警惕
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: Nvidia首席执行官黄仁勋与一名被指控为北京从事间谍活动的中国女子的暧昧关系，已成为美国的一项重大国家安全关切。据美国情报官员透露，Alice Huang曾于2023年在总部位于新加坡的数据中心企业Megaspeed担任业务主管，据称她收集情报并将其传递给中国。这场丑闻正值美国与中国竞逐全球人工智能领导地位之际爆发。曾任国家情报院院长的退休情报官员 Yoo Seong-ok 在其国家情报院（NIS）任职期间警告称，韩国同样容易受到外国情报机构的间谍活动渗透，这些机构意图窃取关键技术。他告诉《韩国时报》：“中国或朝鲜间谍，或两者都有，可能曾使用、或至今仍在使用与据称针对Nvidia首席执行官黄仁勋所设的类似的蜜罐，以收集机密信息并传递给各自的情报机构。”更值得注意的是，Yoo指出，鉴于Nvidia与韩国两家芯片制造商关系密切，有关Samsung Electronics、SK hynix及其技术的敏感信息可能已经传递给中国的竞争对手。黄仁勋曾以被称为“AI伙伴联盟”的机制，多次与Samsung Electronics董事长李在镕和SK hynix董事长崔泰源会面，会面地点包括韩国和美国。Yoo说：“据媒体报道，Nvidia首席执行官与Alice Huang关系亲密。他在与该女子交谈时，可能无意中分享了与韩国商界领袖会面的细节。谁知道呢？”韩国有充分理由成为外国间谍活动的目标。其制造企业在全球人工智能产业中发挥关键作用，为人工智能计算提供核心组件。Samsung Electronics和SK hynix主导高带宽存储器（HBM）市场，合计占全球市场份额的80%以上。两家公司对全球人工智能供应链具有战略重要性，因此它们及其最高管理层都可能成为外国情报行动的目标。近年来，全球情报界已呈现出明显趋势：各国正加强情报能力，以应对不断演变的安全挑战。欧盟委员会正考虑在Ursula von der Leyen总统领导下设立一个情报机构，以应对人工智能时代的技术和地缘政治挑战。日本也采取了类似措施，自首相Sanae Takaichi上任以来推进国家安全和情报体系改革。该国还成立了国家情报委员会，负责监督其情报战略。今年8月，国防反情报司令部被解散；此前一年多前，该机构曾介入前总统Yoon Suk Yeol于2024年12月3日宣布戒严一事。自2024年1月将侦查和调查间谍案件的权限移交给警方后，NIS的反情报能力也明显削弱。Yoo说：“从那以后，没有一名朝鲜间谍被抓捕。这表明，该国在反情报方面几乎没有采取任何行动。”Jang表达了类似担忧。他指出，为应对不断变化的安全环境，世界各国都在加强情报收集和分析活动。他说：“中国、俄罗斯和朝鲜等国家加大了间谍行动力度，以获取关键技术和情报。在这种情况下，韩国采取的做法很难说得通。”Jang还警告称，半导体以外的其他战略部门，尤其是国防工业，正日益成为外国间谍活动的目标。他强调，韩国必须紧急加强反情报能力，以保护其战略技术、产业资产和国家安全

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body: Participants from Mexico to Uzbekistan immerse themselves in language workshops, traditional cuisine, classic poetry Ninety-two students and teachers from 30 countries wrapped up a five-day immersive camp hosted by the Ministry of Education. A group of 92 secondary school students and teachers from 30 countries completed a five-day immersive journey into Korean language and culture, concluding a nationwide youth camp organized by the Ministry of Education. To mark the end of the 2026 International Korean Education Youth Camp, the ministry and the International Korean Education Foundation held a celebratory ceremony Tuesday evening at Sarangjae, a traditional guest house on the National Assembly grounds in Seoul. Running from Friday to Tuesday across Seoul and Incheon, the camp brought together students enrolled in Korean language classes at their home schools. This year’s cohort welcomed its first-ever participant from Mexico, alongside students from Malaysia and Uzbekistan who were recently featured in a KBS documentary aired on Hangeul Day, the Oct. 9 national holiday celebrating the Korean alphabet. During the program, participants engaged in level-tailored Korean lessons leveraging artificial intelligence. Beyond the classroom, they explored historic landmarks, including Gyeongbok Palace, the main royal palace of the 1392-1910 Joseon Dynasty, and sampled iconic street foods like "tteokbokki," Korea’s signature spicy simmered rice cakes. The students also studied "Sejong 1446" — a musical depicting King Sejong’s 15th-century creation of Hangeul — and prepared a live performance for the closing ceremony. The camp featured a literature contest where students recited and interpreted works from Korean school textbooks, with Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin on hand to present awards to the top three finalists. Phung Khanh Linh of Vietnam presented Yi Chong-jun’s classic 1977 short story “The Snowy Road," a textbook staple exploring themes of maternal sacrifice and unpayable filial debt through the memory of a mother walking her son to the bus along a snow-covered mountain path. Siriwardena Chanthuki Thathyana of Sri Lanka recited Hwang Ji-u’s famous 1997 poem “While Waiting for You," a staple of Korean literature that frames waiting not as passive resignation, but as an active, urgent journey of love toward an inevitable arrival. Prasista Zharafah Mulia of Indonesia performed Oh Sae-young’s lyric poem “Like a Star, Like a Flower," which uses vivid natural imagery to reflect on living a pure, illuminating life despite transient worldly hardship. Reflecting on her selection, the Sri Lankan student shared that she viewed the "you" in Hwang's poem as representing Korea itself — explaining that rather than passively waiting for a dream to materialize, she felt inspired to actively pursue and create her own opportunities. Launched in 2019 as a regional exchange with Southeast Asian nations, the program expanded globally in 2022 to welcome Korean language learners worldwide. “Meeting peers from around the world here in Korea will serve as powerful motivation for these students to continue their language journey,” Choi said. “I hope they grow into global leaders who maintain strong ties with Korea.” This article was published with the assistance of generative AI and edited by The Korea Times
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.title_zh: 来自30个国家的学生齐聚首尔学习韩语和韩国文化
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body_zh: 来自墨西哥至乌兹别克斯坦等国的参与者沉浸式学习韩语课程、传统美食和经典诗歌。由教育部主办的为期五天的沉浸式夏令营落下帷幕，来自30个国家的92名中学生和教师完成了为期五天的韩国语言与文化沉浸体验，结束了教育部组织的全国青少年夏令营。为纪念2026年国际韩国教育青少年夏令营闭幕，教育部与国际韩国教育基金会于周二晚上在首尔国会议事堂 grounds 内的传统客栈 Sarangjae 举行庆祝仪式。夏令营从周五持续至周二，贯穿首尔和仁川，吸引了各国本土学校韩语课程的学生参加。今年的参与者中首次欢迎了来自墨西哥的学员，此外还有来自马来西亚和乌兹别克斯坦的学生；这些学生近期出现在 KBS 于10月9日韩文日这一庆祝韩文字母的韩国国庆日播出的纪录片中。活动期间，参与者参加了根据不同水平设计的韩语课程，并利用人工智能开展学习。课堂之外，他们参观了历史遗迹，包括1392年至1910年朝鲜王朝的主要王宫景福宫，还品尝了韩式辣炒年糕等韩国代表性街头小吃，以“떡볶이”（“韩式辣炒年糕”）为代表。学生们还学习了音乐剧《世宗1446》，该剧描绘了世宗大王于15世纪创制训民正音（韩文）的历史，并为闭幕式准备了一场现场演出。夏令营还举办了文学比赛，学生们诵读并解读韩国学校教科书中的作品，教育部长崔教振现场为决赛前三名颁奖。越南的 Phung Khanh Linh 讲解了李忠俊1977年的经典短篇小说《雪路》，这篇课文常见作品通过儿子在积雪覆盖的山路上走向公交车站的母亲这一回忆，探讨母爱牺牲与无法偿还的孝亲之恩等主题。斯里兰卡的 Siriwardena Chanthuki Thathyana 诵读了黄智宇1997年的著名诗作《在等待你的日子里》，这首作品是韩国文学的经典，将等待塑造成不是被动 resignation，而是通向必然重逢的积极而急迫的爱之旅。印度尼西亚的 Prasista Zharafah Mulia 表演了吴世永的抒情诗《如星，如花》，以生动的自然意象反思如何在短暂的世界苦难中过上纯净、照亮他人的生活。回顾自己入选的原因，斯里兰卡学生表示，她把黄智宇诗中的“你”理解为韩国本身，并解释说，梦想不会被动地等待实现，这促使她受到启发，主动追求并创造属于自己的机会。该项目于2019年作为与东南亚国家之间的区域交流项目启动，2022年扩大至全球范围，迎来世界各地的韩语学习者。崔教振表示：“这些学生在这里与世界各地的同龄人相会，将成为他们继续学习语言的强大动力。”“我希望他们成长为与韩国保持密切联系的全球领袖。”本文在生成式人工智能的协助下完成，并由《韩国时报》编辑。

https://leadership.ng/nigeria-proposes-l.summary: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, disclosed this on Tuesday at the S&P Global Ratings Africa Summit in Lagos, where he said fragmented capital markets across the region were limiting access to the scale of financing required to support economic development.
https://leadership.ng/nigeria-proposes-l.summary_zh: 财政部长兼经济协调部长泰沃·奥耶德莱周二在拉各斯举行的S&P Global Ratings Africa Summit上披露了这一情况。他表示，该地区碎片化的资本市场正在限制融资规模，使支持经济发展所需的融资难以获得。
https://leadership.ng/nigeria-proposes-l.body: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, disclosed this on Tuesday at the S&P Global Ratings Africa Summit in Lagos, where he said fragmented capital markets across the region were limiting access to the scale of financing required to support economic development. Oyedele said no single market in the region was sufficiently deep to attract the volume of long-term investments needed to fund infrastructure and drive sustainable growth, making greater cooperation among countries imperative. Under the proposed framework, Nigeria is advocating a regional capital market passport regime that would allow issuers approved in one participating country to raise funds across other markets without undergoing separate regulatory approval processes. The proposal also includes a unified investor identification system that would enable investors registered in one market to purchase bonds and equities across the region without repeating registration and onboarding requirements. The minister said Nigeria was equally pushing for the integration of regional trading, settlement and payment infrastructure to enable securities transactions to be settled directly in local currencies, thereby reducing dependence on the United States dollar. The proposed integration would cover Nigeria, Ghana and eight francophone countries that share the CFA franc and a common central bank. They are Benin, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo. Oyedele said existing regional initiatives, including the West African Capital Markets Integration Council, the African Exchanges Linkage Project and the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), provided a foundation for the proposed integration. “The task now is to join these pieces together,” he said. Beyond removing regulatory and operational barriers, the proposed reforms would include the development of a regional local-currency bond index and a credit enhancement facility to support cross-border infrastructure financing. The credit enhancement facility is expected to strengthen the capacity of countries to attract long-term capital for projects that may otherwise struggle to secure funding from individual domestic markets. Oyedele said the broader objective was to create a more integrated investment environment that would attract domestic and foreign investors while improving access to capital across the region. He also disclosed that Nigeria was targeting investment-grade credit ratings within three years as part of efforts to strengthen investor confidence and improve the country’s access to international capital. The minister said the government was working towards building a capital market worth at least $1 trillion under its 10-year capital market plan. The proposed regional integration is expected to expand investment opportunities beyond national borders, allowing issuers to access a wider pool of investors and providing investors with more opportunities to deploy capital across West Africa.
